§6.3 Line Separators and Breaks

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

layout-line-separators-and-breaks · rule layout model-divergence

✅ Normative

A printed section separator MUST be rendered as <hr/>, at its place in reading order. --- MUST NOT be used for it: --- is reserved for page boundaries. A rule MUST NOT be inserted where the page prints only whitespace.

A horizontal rule or separator printed between sections of a page. It is printed content: it tells a reader that one block has ended and another begun, so it survives into the output.

… end of the first section.
────────────────────────────        ← printed rule between sections  →  <hr/>
Start of the next section …

Requirements

  • Each printed separator between sections MUST produce one <hr/> line, placed between the elements it separates in reading order.
  • The separator MUST NOT be written as ---, ***, ___ or any other Markdown thematic break.
  • Vertical whitespace between sections, with no printed line, MUST NOT produce <hr/>.

Why never ---

--- is already load-bearing twice. It is the page-break marker of Markdown Rendering§3.2, and at the top of a file it opens frontmatter. A separator that renders identically to a page break makes page attribution ambiguous for anything splitting on it, and can silently truncate a document at the top of a file. <hr/> avoids both collisions and follows the general posture of falling back to HTML wherever a Markdown spelling is ambiguous — see Text Formatting Conventions§7.1.

Related
